raw_response:
I have been growing cotton on these 3 mu for fifty years, and I know what works here in Quzhou. Last year I planted the improved Guoxinmian seeds that my neighbor Lao Zhang uses, and I got about 400 jin of seed cotton per mu. This year I will do the same — I will buy 2 jin of seed per mu from the dealer in Anzhai town.

For fertilizer, I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu when I prepare the land. One bag is 50 kg, the 15-15-15 kind that costs about 130 yuan. That gives me roughly 7 to 8 kg each of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium per mu. Then when the cotton starts flowering in July, I topdress with urea — about 30 kg per mu total, split into two times. The dealer told me the urea is 46% nitrogen, so I figure that is about 22 kg of nitrogen per mu altogether. I would rather spend the extra 40 yuan per mu on fertilizer than risk a bad harvest. Last year I cut back on the urea and my yield dropped by nearly 50 kg per mu. My grandson is still in school and I need the cash.

I irrigate three times from my well. Once right after sowing in late April, once when the flowers open in July, and once in August when the bolls are filling. Each time I run the pump for about two hours. Electricity costs money, so I do not water more than that, but three times is enough if the rains are normal.

Cotton bollworm is my biggest enemy. I spray pesticide about 10 times from June to September. I use whatever the dealer recommends — usually a pyrethroid mixed with something else. Each spray costs me about 12 to 15 yuan per mu for the chemical, plus my own labor with the backpack sprayer. I cannot skip sprays because one week of bollworm will eat my whole crop.

I use rotary tillage. My son-in-law brings his small tractor and we finish my 3 mu in one morning. It costs me 40 yuan per mu.

I expect about 450 kg of seed cotton per mu this year if the weather is normal. That should give me enough to cover inputs and still have cash left for the family.
